records.context: Annotation is the bottleneck in every screen. An extracted image region the model already calls with 0.999 teaches the model nothing when a human labels it; the extracted image regions worth a person's afternoon are the ones sitting on the decision boundary. This module turns an already-scored ``measurements.db`` into a work list ordered so the informative extracted image regions come first.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Annotation is the bottleneck in every screen. A crop the model already calls with 0.999 teaches the model nothing when a human labels it; the crops worth a person's afternoon are the ones sitting on the decision boundary. This module turns an already-scored ``measurements.db`` into a work queue ordered so the informative crops come first.
records.translation: La anotación es el cuello de botella de todo cribado. Un recorte que el modelo ya clasifica con 0.999 no le enseña nada cuando una persona lo etiqueta; los recortes que merecen la tarde de una persona son los que se encuentran en la frontera de decisión. Este módulo convierte un ``measurements.db`` ya puntuado en una cola de trabajo ordenada de modo que los recortes informativos aparezcan primero.

records.context: **Uncertainty sampling skews toward the majority class.** On a screen that is 98 % negative, the decision boundary is mostly populated by negatives, so the annotation work list will be too. The annotation work list summary reports this as a class-balance table so the annotator can cap or rebalance the annotation work list.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Uncertainty sampling skews toward the majority class.** On a screen that is 98 % negative, the decision boundary is mostly populated by negatives, so the queue will be too. The queue summary reports this as a class-balance table so the annotator can cap or rebalance the queue.
records.translation: **El muestreo por incertidumbre se sesga hacia la clase mayoritaria.** En un cribado que es negativo en un 98 %, la frontera de decisión está poblada sobre todo por negativos, y la cola también lo estará. El resumen de la cola lo notifica como una tabla de equilibrio de clases para que el anotador pueda limitar o reequilibrar la cola.

records.context: **A softmax is not a probability.** Everything here is called an uncertainty *score*, never a confidence. Modern networks are badly calibrated — typically over-confident, and more so the deeper they are (Guo et al., 2017) — so a 0.87 from the head is not "87 % sure". The scores are used for one thing only: putting extracted image regions in an order. Nothing in this module reports a calibrated probability, and neither should anything built on it. See :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A softmax is not a probability.** Everything here is called an uncertainty *score*, never a confidence. Modern networks are badly calibrated — typically over-confident, and more so the deeper they are (Guo et al., 2017) — so a 0.87 from the head is not "87 % sure". The scores are used for one thing only: putting crops in an order. Nothing in this module reports a calibrated probability, and neither should anything built on it. See :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.
records.translation: **Una softmax no es una probabilidad.** Todo aquí se denomina *puntuación* de incertidumbre, nunca confianza. Las redes modernas están mal calibradas (normalmente con exceso de confianza, y más cuanto más profundas son; Guo et al., 2017), de modo que un 0.87 de la cabeza no significa "87 % sure". Las puntuaciones se usan para una sola cosa: ordenar recortes. Nada en este módulo informa de una probabilidad calibrada, y nada construido sobre él debería hacerlo. Véase :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.

records.context: **Already-annotated extracted image regions never enter the annotation work list.** ``NULL`` in the annotation column is the abstention marker — the extracted image region has not been looked at. ``0`` is a real class, and an annotation work list that re-serves it wastes exactly the resource this module exists to save. The two are distinguished by ``IS NULL``, never by falsiness. (Same convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)
records.label: spacr.active_learning#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Already-annotated crops never enter the queue.** ``NULL`` in the annotation column is the abstention marker — the crop has not been looked at. ``0`` is a real class, and a queue that re-serves it wastes exactly the resource this module exists to save. The two are distinguished by ``IS NULL``, never by falsiness. (Same convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)
records.translation: **Los recortes ya anotados nunca entran en la cola.** ``NULL`` en la columna de anotación es el marcador de abstención: el recorte no se ha revisado. ``0`` es una clase real, y una cola que lo vuelve a servir desperdicia exactamente el recurso que este módulo existe para ahorrar. Ambos se distinguen mediante ``IS NULL``, nunca por su valor de verdad. (Misma convención que :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)

records.context: **The two head shapes are handled separately.** The machine-learning classification model head emits either a single logit (binary; needs a sigmoid) or C logits (multiclass; needs a softmax) — see :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Pushing a single-logit column through a softmax yields a column of 1.0 and destroys the ordering; pushing C logits through a sigmoid can *invert* it. Both are silent failures that produce a confident-looking work list full of nonsense, so :func:`probabilities_from_logits` branches on the shape and the tests pin both directions.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The two head shapes are handled separately.** The classifier head emits either a single logit (binary; needs a sigmoid) or C logits (multiclass; needs a softmax) — see :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Pushing a single-logit column through a softmax yields a column of 1.0 and destroys the ordering; pushing C logits through a sigmoid can *invert* it. Both are silent failures that produce a confident-looking queue full of nonsense, so :func:`probabilities_from_logits` branches on the shape and the tests pin both directions.
records.translation: **Las dos formas de cabeza se tratan por separado.** La cabeza del clasificador emite un único logit (binario; necesita una sigmoide) o C logits (multiclase; necesita una softmax); véase :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Pasar una columna de un único logit por una softmax produce una columna de 1.0 y destruye la ordenación; pasar C logits por una sigmoide puede *invertirla*. Ambos son fallos silenciosos que producen una cola de apariencia fiable llena de sinsentidos, por lo que :func:`probabilities_from_logits` bifurca según la forma y las pruebas fijan ambos sentidos.

records.source: The distribution of labels across experimental units determines whether a classifier can generalize beyond acquisition-specific staining, focus and confluency. A label set concentrated within one well can therefore yield optimistic performance under an object-level random split. This function exposes such concentration before model training or evaluation.
records.translation: La distribución de las etiquetas entre unidades experimentales determina si un clasificador puede generalizar más allá de la tinción, el enfoque y la confluencia propios de una adquisición. Por ello, un conjunto de etiquetas concentrado en un solo pocillo puede dar un rendimiento optimista con una división aleatoria a nivel de objeto. Esta función pone de manifiesto esa concentración antes del entrenamiento o la evaluación del modelo.

If the column does not exist at all, nothing has been annotated yet and every crop is queued (with a note saying so). This is the same abstention convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.
records.translation: **Se excluyen los recortes ya anotados.** ``NULL`` en ``annotation_column`` significa "not looked at"; cualquier otro valor, *incluido 0*, significa que una persona se decidió por una clase. Si la columna no existe en absoluto, aún no se ha anotado nada y todos los recortes entran en la cola (con una nota que lo indica). Es la misma convención de abstención que :mod:`spacr.agreement`.

records.context: **The annotation work list is diversified by default, and that costs something.** With ``diversity='well'`` the ranked extracted image regions are dealt round-robin across microplate sample positions: position 1 is still the single most uncertain extracted image region, but position 2 is the most uncertain extracted image region in a *different* well, which may be materially less uncertain than the runner-up overall. You give up some per-item uncertainty to stop the annotator labelling the same ambiguity a hundred times — the failure mode of pure uncertainty sampling, where the top 100 extracted image regions routinely come from two microplate sample positions. If ``limit`` is smaller than the number of microplate sample positions, the annotation work list will contain roughly one extracted image region from each of ``limit`` microplate sample positions and none from the rest. Pass ``diversity='none'`` for the pure order, ``'field'``/``'plate'`` for other strata, or ``group_columns=[…]`` for your own — including a cluster id you computed from features, which is the more thorough diversification this trades away for not needing a feature matrix.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.build_queue#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The queue is diversified by default, and that costs something.** With ``diversity='well'`` the ranked crops are dealt round-robin across wells: position 1 is still the single most uncertain crop, but position 2 is the most uncertain crop in a *different* well, which may be materially less uncertain than the runner-up overall. You give up some per-item uncertainty to stop the annotator labelling the same ambiguity a hundred times — the failure mode of pure uncertainty sampling, where the top 100 crops routinely come from two wells. If ``limit`` is smaller than the number of wells, the queue will contain roughly one crop from each of ``limit`` wells and none from the rest. Pass ``diversity='none'`` for the pure order, ``'field'``/``'plate'`` for other strata, or ``group_columns=[…]`` for your own — including a cluster id you computed from features, which is the more thorough diversification this trades away for not needing a feature matrix.
records.translation: **Por defecto, la cola se diversifica, y eso tiene un coste.** Con ``diversity='well'``, los recortes ordenados se reparten por turnos entre pocillos: la posición 1 sigue siendo el recorte más incierto de todos, pero la posición 2 es el recorte más incierto de un pocillo *distinto*, que puede ser bastante menos incierto que el segundo en la clasificación global. Se renuncia a parte de la incertidumbre por elemento para evitar que el anotador etiquete la misma ambigüedad cien veces, el modo de fallo del muestreo por incertidumbre puro, en el que los 100 primeros recortes proceden habitualmente de dos pocillos. Si ``limit`` es menor que el número de pocillos, la cola contendrá aproximadamente un recorte de cada uno de ``limit`` pocillos y ninguno del resto. Pase ``diversity='none'`` para el orden puro, ``'field'``/``'plate'`` para otros estratos o ``group_columns=[…]`` para los suyos propios, incluido un identificador de clúster calculado a partir de características, que es la diversificación más exhaustiva a la que esto renuncia a cambio de no necesitar una matriz de características.

An ensemble — several checkpoints, several folds, or several MC-dropout passes of one model — separates those: crops the members *disagree* about are where the model class itself is undecided (epistemic uncertainty), which is what a new label actually fixes.
records.translation: Las medidas anteriores ven la opinión de un solo modelo y llaman "uncertain" a una salida 50/50, tanto si el modelo está realmente dividido como si simplemente está mal calibrado. Un conjunto de modelos (varios puntos de control, varios pliegues o varias pasadas de MC-dropout de un mismo modelo) los separa: los recortes sobre los que los miembros *discrepan* son aquellos en los que la propia clase de modelos está indecisa (incertidumbre epistémica), que es lo que realmente corrige una nueva etiqueta.

records.translation: ``(N,)`` o ``(N, 1)``: una **cabeza binaria de un único logit**. Sigmoide y, después, expansión a ``[1 − p, p]`` para que todas las medidas vean dos clases. records.source: Why this rule and not another:
records.translation: Por qué esta regla y no otra:

records.context: **Labels, not rounds, are the unit of cost.** A round is whatever size the annotator felt like; "no improvement for 3 rounds" says nothing when the rounds were 5, 300 and 8 labels. The thing being spent is human attention, one extracted image region at a time, so the window is measured in extracted image regions.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Labels, not rounds, are the unit of cost.** A round is whatever size the annotator felt like; "no improvement for 3 rounds" says nothing when the rounds were 5, 300 and 8 labels. The thing being spent is human attention, one crop at a time, so the window is measured in crops.
records.translation: **La unidad de coste son las etiquetas, no las rondas.** Una ronda tiene el tamaño que le apeteció al anotador; "no improvement for 3 rounds" no dice nada cuando las rondas fueron de 5, 300 y 8 etiquetas. Lo que se gasta es atención humana, un recorte cada vez, por lo que la ventana se mide en recortes.

records.context: **It looks *back over* rounds, not *at* the last one.** A single round that happened to land flat is noise; the question is whether the last fifty labels — however they were divided up — bought anything.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It looks *back over* rounds, not *at* the last one.** A single round that happened to land flat is noise; the question is whether the last fifty labels — however they were divided up — bought anything.
records.translation: **Mira *hacia atrás a lo largo de* las rondas, no *a* la última.** Una sola ronda que resultó plana es ruido; la pregunta es si las últimas cincuenta etiquetas, como quiera que se repartieran, aportaron algo.

records.context: **It refuses to answer early.** Below ``label_window`` labels since the first recorded round there is no window to measure, and a rule that fired anyway would tell people to stop after their first twelve labels.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It refuses to answer early.** Below ``label_window`` labels since the first recorded round there is no window to measure, and a rule that fired anyway would tell people to stop after their first twelve labels.
records.translation: **Se niega a responder antes de tiempo.** Por debajo de ``label_window`` etiquetas desde la primera ronda registrada no hay ninguna ventana que medir, y una regla que se activara de todos modos diría a la gente que parase tras sus doce primeras etiquetas.

records.context: **It distinguishes "flat" from "unmeasurable".** Held-out accuracy on 80 objects has a standard error near 0.05; a 0.3 % change is inside the noise, and :attr:`StoppingVerdict.confident` says so instead of dressing it up. Flat *is* still the recommendation — if more labels are not moving a number you can measure, they are not buying anything you can demonstrate — but the reason says the held-out set is too small to prove convergence, which is a different piece of work.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It distinguishes "flat" from "unmeasurable".** Held-out accuracy on 80 objects has a standard error near 0.05; a 0.3 % change is inside the noise, and :attr:`StoppingVerdict.confident` says so instead of dressing it up. Flat *is* still the recommendation — if more labels are not moving a number you can measure, they are not buying anything you can demonstrate — but the reason says the held-out set is too small to prove convergence, which is a different piece of work.
records.translation: **Distingue "flat" de "unmeasurable".** La exactitud en un conjunto reservado de 80 objetos tiene un error estándar cercano a 0.05; un cambio del 0.3 % está dentro del ruido, y :attr:`StoppingVerdict.confident` lo indica en lugar de disimularlo. Plano *sigue siendo* la recomendación (si más etiquetas no mueven un número que se pueda medir, no aportan nada que se pueda demostrar), pero el motivo indica que el conjunto reservado es demasiado pequeño para demostrar la convergencia, lo cual es otro trabajo distinto.

records.context: **A falling curve stops too, and says so.** Accuracy going down is not convergence; it usually means the newest labels disagree with the earlier ones, or that the held-out split moved. Either way, more of the same is the wrong next move.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A falling curve stops too, and says so.** Accuracy going down is not convergence; it usually means the newest labels disagree with the earlier ones, or that the held-out split moved. Either way, more of the same is the wrong next move.
records.translation: **Una curva descendente también detiene, y lo dice.** Que la exactitud baje no es convergencia; normalmente significa que las etiquetas más recientes discrepan de las anteriores o que la división reservada cambió. En cualquier caso, seguir haciendo lo mismo es el paso siguiente equivocado.

records.source: The input consists of a guide- or gene-level coefficient, per-object measurements and per-well guide fractions. Because pooled screens do not identify which individual cell contains a guide, the result represents cells whose measured phenotype is consistent with the fitted effect; it does not assign a genotype to individual cells. :class:`MontagePlan` includes :data:`INFERENCE_NOTICE` in every generated caption to preserve this distinction.
records.translation: La entrada consiste en un coeficiente a nivel de guía o de gen, mediciones por objeto y fracciones de guía por pocillo. Como los cribados agrupados no identifican qué célula individual contiene una guía, el resultado representa células cuyo fenotipo medido es coherente con el efecto ajustado; no asigna un genotipo a células individuales. :class:`MontagePlan` incluye :data:`INFERENCE_NOTICE` en cada pie generado para preservar esta distinción.

records.context: Selection proceeds in three stages:
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Selection proceeds in three stages:
records.translation: La selección se realiza en tres etapas:

records.context: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifies microplate sample positions with a non-zero fraction of the guide or gene. Gene-level selection sums guide fractions by default; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evaluates guides separately. 2. :func:`score_window` defines ``target = baseline + effect`` and retains objects within ``half_widths`` robust scales of the target, ordered by ``|score - target|``. The baseline and scale are calculated across the supplied object population rather than separately for each gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selects ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objects from each microplate sample position. Zero-contribution microplate sample positions remain in the plan for reporting.
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifies wells with a non-zero fraction of the guide or gene. Gene-level selection sums guide fractions by default; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evaluates guides separately. 2. :func:`score_window` defines ``target = baseline + effect`` and retains objects within ``half_widths`` robust scales of the target, ordered by ``|score - target|``. The baseline and scale are calculated across the supplied object population rather than separately for each gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selects ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objects from each well. Zero-contribution wells remain in the plan for reporting.
records.translation: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifica los pocillos con una fracción no nula de la guía o del gen. La selección a nivel de gen suma por defecto las fracciones de las guías; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evalúa las guías por separado. 2. :func:`score_window` define ``target = baseline + effect`` y conserva los objetos que están a menos de ``half_widths`` escalas robustas del objetivo, ordenados por ``|score - target|``. La línea base y la escala se calculan sobre toda la población de objetos suministrada y no por separado para cada gen. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selecciona ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objetos de cada pocillo. Los pocillos sin contribución permanecen en el plan a efectos de información.

So the frame that comes back serves **both** crop sources: ``png_path`` for :class:`~spacr.crops.PngCropSource`, ``path_name`` plus ``object_label`` for :class:`~spacr.crops.MergedCropSource`.

Así, la tabla devuelta sirve a **ambas** fuentes de recortes: ``png_path`` para :class:`~spacr.crops.PngCropSource`, ``path_name`` más ``object_label`` para :class:`~spacr.crops.MergedCropSource`.

records.context: This module converts vendor image files into a layout spaCR can read. It is **decoupled from the mask workflow**: nothing here imports torch, cellpose or :mod:`spacr.core`, so it can be executed, tested and previewed on a laptop with no GPU and no segmentation settings in sight.

records.source: This module converts vendor image files into a layout spaCR can read. It is **decoupled from the mask pipeline**: nothing here imports torch, cellpose or :mod:`spacr.core`, so it can be run, tested and previewed on a laptop with no GPU and no segmentation settings in sight.
records.translation: Este módulo convierte archivos de imagen de fabricantes a una estructura que spaCR puede leer. Está **desacoplado de la canalización de máscaras**: nada de lo que hay aquí importa torch, cellpose ni :mod:`spacr.core`, de modo que puede ejecutarse, probarse y previsualizarse en un portátil sin GPU y sin ninguna configuración de segmentación a la vista.

records.context: **Z that is not silently flattened.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` max-projects unconditionally in three of its four branches (ND2, LIF, and both the 3-D and 4-D TIFF cases), and says so nowhere in its output. Here the default is :data:`Z_KEEP` — every image layer is written with its own ``Z##`` — and choosing to project is an explicit ``z_handling='max'``, announced in the plan and recorded per row in the map file.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Z that is not silently flattened.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` max-projects unconditionally in three of its four branches (ND2, LIF, and both the 3-D and 4-D TIFF cases), and says so nowhere in its output. Here the default is :data:`Z_KEEP` — every plane is written with its own ``Z##`` — and choosing to project is an explicit ``z_handling='max'``, announced in the plan and recorded per row in the map file.
records.translation: **Z que no se aplana en silencio.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` hace una proyección de máximos de forma incondicional en tres de sus cuatro ramas (ND2, LIF y los casos TIFF 3-D y 4-D) y no lo indica en ninguna parte de su salida. Aquí, el valor por defecto es :data:`Z_KEEP` (cada plano se escribe con su propio ``Z##``), y elegir proyectar es un ``z_handling='max'`` explícito, anunciado en el plan y registrado por fila en el archivo de mapa.

records.translation: Reglas de diseño

records.context: **No new required dependencies.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` are probed with :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; when one is missing the affected files are reported as skipped with the package name and the ``pip install`` line, never as an ImportError traceback.
records.label: spacr.convert#12
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **No new required dependencies.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` are probed with :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; when one is missing the affected files are reported as skipped with the package name and the ``pip install`` line, never as an ImportError traceback.
records.translation: **Ninguna dependencia obligatoria nueva.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` se sondean con :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; cuando falta uno, los archivos afectados se notifican como omitidos con el nombre del paquete y la línea de ``pip install``, nunca como una traza de ImportError.

records.context: **Never overwrite.** Two sources landing on one target name is a *plan-time error* naming both, not a last-writer-wins at convert time. An output that already exists on disk is skipped and counted, so a repeat execution is a no-op rather than a silent rewrite.
records.label: spacr.convert#13
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Never overwrite.** Two sources landing on one target name is a *plan-time error* naming both, not a last-writer-wins at convert time. An output that already exists on disk is skipped and counted, so a re-run is a no-op rather than a silent rewrite.
records.translation: **Nunca sobrescribir.** Que dos orígenes vayan a parar a un mismo nombre de destino es un *error en el momento de la planificación* que nombra a ambos, no una regla de que gana el último en escribir en el momento de la conversión. Una salida que ya existe en disco se omite y se contabiliza, de modo que repetir la ejecución no hace nada en lugar de reescribir en silencio.

records.context: **Atomic writes.** Every TIFF is written to a temp file in the destination and :func:`os.replace`\ d into place, so an interrupted run leaves no half-written file that the next run mistakes for done.
records.label: spacr.convert#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Atomic writes.** Every TIFF is written to a temp file in the destination and :func:`os.replace`\ d into place, so an interrupted run leaves no half-written file that the next run mistakes for done.
records.translation: **Escrituras atómicas.** Cada TIFF se escribe en un archivo temporal en el destino y se coloca en su sitio con :func:`os.replace`, de modo que una ejecución interrumpida no deja ningún archivo a medio escribir que la siguiente ejecución tome por terminado.

records.context: :func:`spacr.io.convert_to_yokogawa` already converts ND2/CZI/LIF/TIFF, and it is still the right tool when you want an in-place rename of a flat folder. It does not provide the three features of this module:

records.source: :func:`spacr.io.convert_to_yokogawa` already converts ND2/CZI/LIF/TIFF, and it is still the right tool when you want an in-place rename of a flat folder. It does not provide the three features of this module:
records.translation: :func:`spacr.io.convert_to_yokogawa` ya convierte ND2/CZI/LIF/TIFF, y sigue siendo la herramienta adecuada cuando se desea renombrar en el sitio una carpeta plana. No ofrece las tres funciones de este módulo:

records.context: **Preview.** It writes as it walks. There is no point at which you can look at "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" and say no. :func:`plan` produces that table and writes nothing.

records.source: **Preview.** It writes as it walks. There is no point at which you can look at "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" and say no. :func:`plan` produces that table and writes nothing.
records.translation: **Vista previa.** Escribe a medida que recorre. No hay ningún momento en el que pueda mirarse "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" y decir que no. :func:`plan` genera esa tabla y no escribe nada.

records.context: **A map you can read back.** It writes a ``rename_log.csv`` whose columns differ per input format (the LIF and TIFF branches record two columns; the ND2 branch records seven; the CZI branch records nine), and nothing in spaCR ever reads it. :func:`write_map` emits one fixed schema and :func:`read_map` / :func:`populate_db_from_map` read it back, so after a run the original filename for any measurement is one SQL join away.

records.translation: **Un mapa que se puede volver a leer.** Escribe un ``rename_log.csv`` cuyas columnas varían según el formato de entrada (las ramas LIF y TIFF registran dos columnas; la rama ND2, siete; la rama CZI, nueve), y nada en spaCR lo lee nunca. :func:`write_map` emite un único esquema fijo y :func:`read_map` / :func:`populate_db_from_map` lo vuelven a leer, de modo que, tras una ejecución, el nombre de archivo original de cualquier medición está a una unión SQL de distancia.

Image Lab stores ``zero_is="white"`` data, so such an image is inverted as ``data_ceiling - raw``; the result then looks like Image Lab's own PDF and TIFF exports (dark objects on a light background). ``zero_is="black"`` data is returned as stored.
records.translation: Solo numpy y la biblioteca estándar: el archivo es un documento MIME multiparte cuyas partes ``ScanImageTagN`` contienen cada una un ``ImageData`` bruto (anchura x altura en uint16 con el orden de bytes indicado) y un ``ImageHeader`` XML. Image Lab almacena datos ``zero_is="white"``, por lo que una imagen así se invierte como ``data_ceiling - raw``; el resultado tiene entonces el mismo aspecto que las exportaciones PDF y TIFF del propio Image Lab (objetos oscuros sobre fondo claro). Los datos ``zero_is="black"`` se devuelven tal como están almacenados.

This module reports where the space in a project is used, and clears derived data without touching the raw microscope images, which cannot be regenerated.

Este módulo informa de dónde se usa el espacio de un proyecto y elimina los datos derivados sin tocar las imágenes brutas del microscopio, que no pueden regenerarse.

records.context: 1. the registry knows it — anything unregistered is never a candidate; 2. its kind is not an **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): nothing in :mod:`spacr.ports` declares that it produces raw images or sequencing reads, so nothing can make them again; 3. a declared **producing module** exists for its kind, and the module the registry recorded is one of them; 4. that module's **inputs are complete** — every recorded input artifact is still registered and still on disk, and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` says the module could execute in this project right now; 5. it was written by a processing session that **finished** (``status == "complete"``); 6. what is on disk still **fingerprints to what was registered**, so a folder somebody has since dropped a file into is not prunable; 7. it lives **inside the project**, reached without following a symlink; 8. **every** artifact sharing its path passes all of the above — three kinds live in ``measurements.db``, and deleting the file for one of them destroys the other two; 9. no other registered artifact sits inside it or around it, because the bytes belong to the innermost one and a plan must not under-report what it deletes.
records.label: spacr.data_manager#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. the registry knows it — anything unregistered is never a candidate; 2. its kind is not an **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): nothing in :mod:`spacr.ports` declares that it produces raw images or sequencing reads, so nothing can make them again; 3. a declared **producing module** exists for its kind, and the module the registry recorded is one of them; 4. that module's **inputs are complete** — every recorded input artifact is still registered and still on disk, and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` says the module could run in this project right now; 5. it was written by a run that **finished** (``status == "complete"``); 6. what is on disk still **fingerprints to what was registered**, so a folder somebody has since dropped a file into is not prunable; 7. it lives **inside the project**, reached without following a symlink; 8. **every** artifact sharing its path passes all of the above — three kinds live in ``measurements.db``, and deleting the file for one of them destroys the other two; 9. no other registered artifact sits inside it or around it, because the bytes belong to the innermost one and a plan must not under-report what it deletes.
records.translation: 1. el registro lo conoce: nada sin registrar es nunca candidato; 2. su tipo no es un **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): nada en :mod:`spacr.ports` declara que produzca imágenes brutas o lecturas de secuenciación, por lo que nada puede volver a generarlas; 3. existe un **módulo productor** declarado para su tipo, y el módulo que registró el registro es uno de ellos; 4. **las entradas de ese módulo están completas**: cada artefacto de entrada registrado sigue registrado y sigue en disco, y :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` indica que el módulo podría ejecutarse ahora mismo en este proyecto; 5. lo escribió una ejecución que **terminó** (``status == "complete"``); 6. lo que hay en disco **sigue teniendo la huella registrada**, de modo que una carpeta en la que alguien ha dejado un archivo desde entonces no puede eliminarse; 7. se encuentra **dentro del proyecto**, alcanzado sin seguir ningún enlace simbólico; 8. **todos** los artefactos que comparten su ruta cumplen todo lo anterior: tres tipos residen en ``measurements.db``, y eliminar el archivo para uno de ellos destruye los otros dos; 9. ningún otro artefacto registrado se encuentra dentro de él o a su alrededor, porque los bytes pertenecen al más interno y un plan no debe informar de menos de lo que elimina.

records.context: Rule 3 also protects other kinds. ``ports.producers_of`` is empty for ``raw-images`` and ``sequencing-reads``, which is *why* originals are safe — and it is empty today for ``channel-stacks`` too, so ``stack/`` is reported as unregistered bytes and never offered, even though it is one of the largest intermediates. This changes only when a port declares that it produces them.

records.source: Rule 3 also protects other kinds. ``ports.producers_of`` is empty for ``raw-images`` and ``sequencing-reads``, which is *why* originals are safe — and it is empty today for ``channel-stacks`` too, so ``stack/`` is reported as unregistered bytes and never offered, even though it is one of the largest intermediates. This changes only when a port declares that it produces them.
records.translation: La regla 3 también protege otros tipos. ``ports.producers_of`` está vacío para ``raw-images`` y ``sequencing-reads``, que es *por lo que* los originales están a salvo, y hoy también está vacío para ``channel-stacks``, de modo que ``stack/`` se notifica como bytes sin registrar y nunca se ofrece, aunque sea uno de los productos intermedios más grandes. Esto solo cambia cuando un puerto declara que los produce.

records.source: Nothing is deleted without a plan.  :func:`plan_prune` returns exactly what would go and how much it frees; :func:`prune` refuses to run unless it is handed :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, a digest over that exact path set and byte total, so a confirmation cannot authorise a deletion other than the one that was shown.
records.translation: No se elimina nada sin un plan.  :func:`plan_prune` devuelve exactamente lo que se eliminaría y cuánto espacio libera; :func:`prune` se niega a ejecutarse salvo que reciba :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, un resumen de ese conjunto exacto de rutas y del total de bytes, de modo que una confirmación no puede autorizar una eliminación distinta de la que se mostró.

records.context: Deleting is **count first, delete second, verify**. The tree is re-fingerprinted against the plan before anything is removed; the registry write is a count and a write on one predicate, checked for equality and rolled back on any difference. See :func:`_verified_write`.

records.source: Deleting is **count first, delete second, verify**. The tree is re-fingerprinted against the plan before anything is removed; the registry write is a count and a write on one predicate, checked for equality and rolled back on any difference. See :func:`_verified_write`.
records.translation: Eliminar consiste en **contar primero, eliminar después y verificar**. records.source: 1. the confirmation must equal :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, a digest over the plan's exact paths and byte total, so a token cannot authorise a deletion other than the one it was shown for; 2. every candidate is re-fingerprinted and must still match the plan. Any difference — a file added, a file changed, the folder gone — aborts the whole call before a single delete; 3. the registry write happens next, inside one transaction, counted and verified (see :func:`_verified_write`). A mismatch rolls it back and raises with **nothing on disk deleted**; 4. only then are the files removed; 5. every path is checked to be gone afterwards.
records.translation: 1. la confirmación debe ser igual a :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, un resumen de las rutas exactas y del total de bytes del plan, de modo que un token no pueda autorizar una eliminación distinta de aquella para la que se mostró; 2. se vuelve a calcular la huella de cada candidato, que debe seguir coincidiendo con el plan. Cualquier diferencia (un archivo añadido, un archivo modificado, la carpeta desaparecida) anula toda la llamada antes de una sola eliminación; 3. a continuación se realiza la escritura en el registro, dentro de una única transacción, contada y verificada (véase :func:`_verified_write`). Una discrepancia la revierte y genera una excepción **sin haber eliminado nada del disco**; 4. solo entonces se eliminan los archivos; 5. después se comprueba que cada ruta haya desaparecido.

records.source: Purpose
records.translation: Propósito

records.context: ``ari`` — **background is excluded.** The Adjusted Rand Index over two raw label images is dominated by background: a 1400x1400 microscope field of view is ~95 % background, both models agree it is background, and those agreed pairs swamp everything else. Two models that disagree about every single object still score about 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` asserts exactly that number on a microscope field of view where the foreground agreement is 0.0).
records.label: spacr.model_compare#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``ari`` — **background is excluded.** The Adjusted Rand Index over two raw label images is dominated by background: a 1400x1400 field is ~95 % background, both models agree it is background, and those agreed pairs swamp everything else. Two models that disagree about every single object still score about 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` asserts exactly that number on a field where the foreground agreement is 0.0).
records.translation: ``ari``: **se excluye el fondo.** El índice de Rand ajustado sobre dos imágenes de etiquetas brutas está dominado por el fondo: un campo de 1400x1400 es fondo en un ~95 %, ambos modelos coinciden en que es fondo, y esos pares concordantes eclipsan todo lo demás. Dos modelos que discrepan en todos y cada uno de los objetos siguen obteniendo aproximadamente 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` verifica exactamente ese número en un campo en el que la concordancia del primer plano es 0.0).

records.context: So the index is computed over the **union foreground** — the pixels at least one model assigned to an object — with pixels the *other* model left unassigned treated as unclustered singletons rather than as one big background cluster. With background as a single cluster, a model that misses an entire object still scores 1.0, because "one object plus a background blob" and "one object plus a background blob" are the same partition. As singletons, missing half the objects scores 0.50.
records.label: spacr.model_compare#11

records.source: So the index is computed over the **union foreground** — the pixels at least one model assigned to an object — with pixels the *other* model left unassigned treated as unclustered singletons rather than as one big background cluster. With background as a single cluster, a model that misses an entire object still scores 1.0, because "one object plus a background blob" and "one object plus a background blob" are the same partition. As singletons, missing half the objects scores 0.50.
records.translation: Por ello, el índice se calcula sobre el **primer plano de la unión** (los píxeles que al menos un modelo asignó a un objeto), tratando los píxeles que el *otro* modelo dejó sin asignar como elementos aislados sin agrupar y no como un gran grupo de fondo. Con el fondo como un solo grupo, un modelo que pasa por alto un objeto entero sigue obteniendo 1.0, porque "one object plus a background blob" y "one object plus a background blob" son la misma partición. Como elementos aislados, pasar por alto la mitad de los objetos da 0.50.

Both failures are reproduced in the tests. :func:`match_objects` thresholds the IoU matrix and then runs :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` over it, which is also what ``cellpose.metrics`` does.

Ambos fallos se reproducen en las pruebas. :func:`match_objects` umbraliza la matriz de IoU y después ejecuta :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` sobre ella, que es también lo que hace ``cellpose.metrics``.

records.context: The index is taken over the pixels at least one mask assigned to an object. Pixels the other mask left unassigned stay in the sample but belong to no cluster (each is its own singleton), so a model that misses an object is penalised for it — with background as one shared cluster it would not be. Pixels neither mask claimed are dropped entirely: they are the agreement that would otherwise be the whole answer.
records.label: spacr.model_compare.adjusted_rand_index#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The index is taken over the pixels at least one mask assigned to an object. Pixels the other mask left unassigned stay in the sample but belong to no cluster (each is its own singleton), so a model that misses an object is penalised for it — with background as one shared cluster it would not be. Pixels neither mask claimed are dropped entirely: they are the agreement that would otherwise be the whole answer.
records.translation: El índice se calcula sobre los píxeles que al menos una máscara asignó a un objeto. Los píxeles que la otra máscara dejó sin asignar permanecen en la muestra pero no pertenecen a ningún grupo (cada uno es un elemento aislado), de modo que un modelo que pasa por alto un objeto se penaliza por ello, algo que no ocurriría con el fondo como un único grupo compartido. Los píxeles que no reclamó ninguna de las máscaras se descartan por completo: son la concordancia que, de lo contrario, sería toda la respuesta.

records.context: Computed in closed form from the object overlap table. Singleton clusters contribute nothing to any ``C(n, 2)`` term, so the expansion never has to be materialised; the only thing they change is the total pair count, which is taken over the union foreground.
records.label: spacr.model_compare.adjusted_rand_index#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Computed in closed form from the object overlap table. Singleton clusters contribute nothing to any ``C(n, 2)`` term, so the expansion never has to be materialised; the only thing they change is the total pair count, which is taken over the union foreground.
records.translation: Se calcula en forma cerrada a partir de la tabla de solapamiento de objetos. Los grupos de un solo elemento no aportan nada a ningún término ``C(n, 2)``, por lo que nunca hay que materializar la expansión; lo único que cambian es el número total de pares, que se calcula sobre el primer plano de la unión.

records.translation: Bipartita, no voraz. Primero se umbraliza la matriz de IoU (todo lo que está por debajo de ``iou_threshold`` pasa a 0) y después :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` maximiza el IoU total sobre lo que queda, que es el mismo procedimiento que usa ``cellpose.metrics._true_positive``. Tomar la mejor pareja de cada objeto produce asignaciones dobles; tomar pares de forma voraz en orden descendente de IoU puede dejar abandonado un par que la asignación óptima conserva. Ambos casos se ejercitan en las pruebas.

records.source: This module is built around two properties of OME-NGFF.
records.translation: Este módulo se basa en dos propiedades de OME-NGFF.

records.context: **2. Units are translated through an explicit table, and an unknown one is refused.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` is the mapping, written out. A unit that is not in it throws :class:`OmeZarrError`. It would be one line to default to ``"px"`` instead, and that one line is how a 0.65 µm pixel becomes a 0.65 px pixel and every downstream area comes out wrong by a factor of 10^6 — in a column named ``cell_area`` that still looks plausible. The error distinguishes the two cases that need different fixes: a unit NGFF does not define (the file is wrong), and a legal NGFF unit spaCR has no short token for (convert it, e.g. to ``micrometer``).
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#11

records.source: **2. Units are translated through an explicit table, and an unknown one is refused.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` is the mapping, written out. A unit that is not in it raises :class:`OmeZarrError`. It would be one line to default to ``"px"`` instead, and that one line is how a 0.65 µm pixel becomes a 0.65 px pixel and every downstream area comes out wrong by a factor of 10^6 — in a column named ``cell_area`` that still looks plausible. The error distinguishes the two cases that need different fixes: a unit NGFF does not define (the file is wrong), and a legal NGFF unit spaCR has no short token for (convert it, e.g. to ``micrometer``).
records.translation: **2. Las unidades se traducen mediante una tabla explícita, y una desconocida se rechaza.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` es la asociación, escrita de forma explícita. Una unidad que no está en ella genera :class:`OmeZarrError`. Recurrir por defecto a ``"px"`` costaría una sola línea, y esa sola línea es la que convierte un píxel de 0.65 µm en un píxel de 0.65 px y hace que todas las áreas posteriores salgan erróneas en un factor de 10^6, en una columna llamada ``cell_area`` que sigue pareciendo verosímil. El error distingue los dos casos que requieren correcciones distintas: una unidad que NGFF no define (el archivo es erróneo) y una unidad legal de NGFF para la que spaCR no tiene token corto (conviértala, p. ej., a ``micrometer``).

records.context: **3. A missing unit means pixels, and is reported.** An NGFF file whose space axes carry no ``unit`` is legal and common — it is what every tool that never knew the pixel size writes. That reads back as ``units="px"`` with :attr:`OmeZarrImage.units_declared` ``False`` and a :meth:`OmeZarrImage.describe` line that says the file declared none. It is never silently upgraded to µm, and ``"px"`` is never written out as a unit string, because NGFF has no pixel unit: writing a px spacing emits axes with no ``unit``, which is the same convention read back.

It is never silently upgraded to µm, and ``"px"`` is never written out as a unit string, because NGFF has no pixel unit: writing a px spacing emits axes with no ``unit``, which is the same convention read back.
records.translation: **3. Una unidad ausente significa píxeles, y se notifica.** Un archivo NGFF cuyos ejes espaciales no llevan ``unit`` es legal y habitual: es lo que escribe toda herramienta que nunca conoció el tamaño del píxel. Eso se lee de vuelta como ``units="px"`` con :attr:`OmeZarrImage.units_declared` en ``False`` y una línea de :meth:`OmeZarrImage.describe` que indica que el archivo no declaró ninguna. Nunca se convierte en silencio a µm, y ``"px"`` nunca se escribe como cadena de unidad, porque NGFF no tiene unidad de píxel: escribir un espaciado en px emite ejes sin ``unit``, que es la misma convención que se lee de vuelta.

Anything else routes through the same :func:`require_codec` refusal as v2 does. ``.zgroup`` / ``.zarray`` / ``zarr.json`` and the ``zarr_format`` field are read rather than assumed, and an unsupported ``zarr_format`` is refused by number.

records.source: **0.4 is fully implemented** — it is what essentially all real data is in, and it is zarr-format 2. 0.5 (zarr-format 3, metadata under an ``ome`` key in ``zarr.json``) is *tolerated*: its metadata is parsed in full, and its chunks are decoded for the codec chains the standard library can do (``bytes``/``transpose``/``gzip``/``crc32c``). Anything else routes through the same :func:`require_codec` refusal as v2 does. ``.zgroup`` / ``.zarray`` / ``zarr.json`` and the ``zarr_format`` field are read rather than assumed, and an unsupported ``zarr_format`` is refused by number.
records.translation: **0.4 está completamente implementada**: es la versión en la que están prácticamente todos los datos reales, y corresponde a zarr-format 2. 0.5 (zarr-format 3, con los metadatos bajo una clave ``ome`` en ``zarr.json``) se *tolera*: sus metadatos se analizan por completo, y sus fragmentos se decodifican para las cadenas de códecs que puede gestionar la biblioteca estándar (``bytes``/``transpose``/``gzip``/``crc32c``). records.source: Downsampling and pyramid transformations
records.translation: Submuestreo y transformaciones de la pirámide

records.context: Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's ``scale`` multiplied by the cumulative factor 2^k on each downsampled axis. Leaving it at level 0's value is a common NGFF bug — it renders as a pyramid whose coarse levels are a quarter the size of the fine ones and drift off the top-left corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and by a different rule per method: a block mean puts the first output element at the *centre* of the block it averaged, half a level-0 pixel in from the edge, so level *k* is translated by ``scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``; a strided level samples element 0 exactly and is not translated at all. Both are written, and asserted in the tests with the numbers spelled out by hand.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#19
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's ``scale`` multiplied by the cumulative factor 2^k on each downsampled axis. Leaving it at level 0's value is a common NGFF bug — it renders as a pyramid whose coarse levels are a quarter the size of the fine ones and drift off the top-left corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and by a different rule per method: a block mean puts the first output element at the *centre* of the block it averaged, half a level-0 pixel in from the edge, so level *k* is translated by ``scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``; a strided level samples element 0 exactly and is not translated at all. Both are written, and asserted in the tests with the numbers spelled out by hand.
records.translation: El ``scale`` del nivel *k* es el ``scale`` del nivel 0 multiplicado por el factor acumulado 2^k en cada eje submuestreado. Dejarlo con el valor del nivel 0 es un error habitual de NGFF: se representa como una pirámide cuyos niveles gruesos miden una cuarta parte de los finos y se desplazan desde la esquina superior izquierda al hacer zoom. El ``translation`` también se desplaza, y según una regla distinta para cada método: una media por bloques sitúa el primer elemento de salida en el *centro* del bloque que promedió, medio píxel del nivel 0 hacia dentro desde el borde, por lo que el nivel *k* se traslada en ``scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``; un nivel con paso muestrea exactamente el elemento 0 y no se traslada en absoluto. Ambos se escriben, y se verifican en las pruebas con los números detallados a mano.

records.context: **Chunked.** The array is stored as a grid of independently compressed blocks, so a 100 GB plate is readable a tile at a time. Metadata queries read no array data: :func:`read_ome_zarr` opens a handful of small JSON files and returns the levels, their shapes, their voxel sizes and their chunk grids without reading any chunk, and :meth:`OmeZarrImage.read` with a ``region=`` decodes only the chunks that region intersects. Every byte of chunk data in the pure-Python path passes through one function, :func:`_read_chunk_bytes`, and ``tests/test_ome_zarr.py`` counts its calls to check that reads are lazy.

records.source: **Chunked.** The array is stored as a grid of independently compressed blocks, so a 100 GB plate is readable a tile at a time. Metadata queries read no array data: :func:`read_ome_zarr` opens a handful of small JSON files and returns the levels, their shapes, their voxel sizes and their chunk grids without reading any chunk, and :meth:`OmeZarrImage.read` with a ``region=`` decodes only the chunks that region intersects. Every byte of chunk data in the pure-Python path passes through one function, :func:`_read_chunk_bytes`, and ``tests/test_ome_zarr.py`` counts its calls to check that reads are lazy.
records.translation: **Por fragmentos.** La matriz se almacena como una cuadrícula de bloques comprimidos de forma independiente, de modo que una placa de 100 GB puede leerse tesela a tesela. Las consultas de metadatos no leen datos de la matriz: :func:`read_ome_zarr` abre un puñado de archivos JSON pequeños y devuelve los niveles, sus formas, sus tamaños de vóxel y sus cuadrículas de fragmentos sin leer ningún fragmento, y :meth:`OmeZarrImage.read` con un ``region=`` decodifica solo los fragmentos que intersecan esa región. Cada byte de datos de fragmento de la ruta en Python puro pasa por una única función, :func:`_read_chunk_bytes`, y ``tests/test_ome_zarr.py`` cuenta sus llamadas para comprobar que las lecturas son diferidas.

records.context: **Multiscale.** The group holds a resolution pyramid, so drawing a 200 px plate overview does not decode full resolution. :meth:`OmeZarrImage.level_for_size` picks the level, and the per-level ``scale`` transformation is what makes the picked level land in the same world coordinates as level 0.

records.translation: **Multiescala.** El grupo contiene una pirámide de resoluciones, de modo que dibujar una vista general de la placa de 200 px no decodifica la resolución completa. :meth:`OmeZarrImage.level_for_size` elige el nivel, y la transformación ``scale`` por nivel es lo que hace que el nivel elegido quede en las mismas coordenadas del mundo que el nivel 0.

records.context: **The transformations.** Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's multiplied by 2^k on each downsampled axis — writing level 0's scale on every level is a common NGFF bug, and it renders as coarse levels that are a quarter the size of the fine ones and slide off the corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and differently per method: a block mean centres its first output element half a level-0 pixel inside the edge, so level *k* gets ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, while a strided level samples element 0 exactly and keeps ``translate_0``.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr.write_ome_zarr#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The transformations.** Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's multiplied by 2^k on each downsampled axis — writing level 0's scale on every level is a common NGFF bug, and it renders as coarse levels that are a quarter the size of the fine ones and slide off the corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and differently per method: a block mean centres its first output element half a level-0 pixel inside the edge, so level *k* gets ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, while a strided level samples element 0 exactly and keeps ``translate_0``.
records.translation: **Las transformaciones.** El ``scale`` del nivel *k* es el del nivel 0 multiplicado por 2^k en cada eje submuestreado; escribir la escala del nivel 0 en todos los niveles es un error habitual de NGFF, y se representa como niveles gruesos que miden una cuarta parte de los finos y se deslizan fuera de la esquina al hacer zoom. El ``translation`` también se desplaza, y de forma distinta según el método: una media por bloques centra su primer elemento de salida medio píxel del nivel 0 hacia dentro del borde, por lo que el nivel *k* recibe ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, mientras que un nivel con paso muestrea exactamente el elemento 0 y conserva ``translate_0``.

records.context: **Sequencing error** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Both packages treat the read fraction as an exact record of which genotypes were in a microplate sample position. Substitution errors, index hopping, PCR chimeras and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing all credit reads to the wrong gene. Simulating it says the direct dilution is small — but that it silently disables the unidentified-gene check, turning genes that were correctly reported as untested into confident non-hits. On the reference design that costs ten times more than the dilution does. See :func:`misassign_reads`.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate#19
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Sequencing error** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Both packages treat the read fraction as an exact record of which genotypes were in a well. Substitution errors, index hopping, PCR chimeras and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing all credit reads to the wrong gene. Simulating it says the direct dilution is small — but that it silently disables the unidentified-gene check, turning genes that were correctly reported as untested into confident non-hits. On the reference design that costs ten times more than the dilution does. See :func:`misassign_reads`.
records.translation: **Error de secuenciación** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Ambos paquetes tratan la fracción de lecturas como un registro exacto de qué genotipos había en un pocillo. Los errores de sustitución, el salto de índices, las quimeras de PCR y el demultiplexado tolerante a discrepancias atribuyen lecturas al gen equivocado. Simularlo indica que la dilución directa es pequeña, pero que desactiva silenciosamente la comprobación de genes no identificados, convirtiendo genes que se notificaban correctamente como no evaluados en no aciertos aparentemente seguros. En el diseño de referencia, eso cuesta diez veces más que la dilución. Véase :func:`misassign_reads`.

records.context: Neither spaCRPower nor the port had this stage, and its absence is optimistic in a specific way: it makes the read fraction an *exact* measure of which genotypes were in a microplate sample position. In a real amplicon screening experiment it is not. A barcode arrives at the wrong gene through base-call substitutions, index hopping on a patterned flow cell, PCR chimeras across the pooled reaction, and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing — and every one of those mechanisms moves reads *toward the middle*, because the destination is drawn from the whole library rather than from the microplate sample positions the source genotype was actually in.

records.source: Neither spaCRPower nor the port had this stage, and its absence is optimistic in a specific way: it makes the read fraction an *exact* measure of which genotypes were in a well. A barcode arrives at the wrong gene through base-call substitutions, index hopping on a patterned flow cell, PCR chimeras across the pooled reaction, and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing — and every one of those mechanisms moves reads *toward the middle*, because the destination is drawn from the whole library rather than from the wells the source genotype was actually in.
records.translation: Ni spaCRPower ni la adaptación tenían esta etapa, y su ausencia es optimista de una manera concreta: hace que la fracción de lecturas sea una medida *exacta* de qué genotipos había en un pocillo. En un cribado real por amplicones no lo es. Un código de barras llega al gen equivocado por sustituciones en la lectura de bases, saltos de índice en una celda de flujo con patrón, quimeras de PCR en la reacción agrupada y demultiplexado tolerante a discrepancias, y todos esos mecanismos desplazan las lecturas *hacia el centro*, porque el destino se extrae de toda la biblioteca y no de los pocillos en los que realmente estaba el genotipo de origen.

records.context: Mis-assignment gives a gene phantom reads in microplate sample positions it never entered, so the covariate the model regresses positive counts on is a shrunk-toward-uniform version of the truth. The obvious consequence is regression dilution — an attenuated coefficient and a smaller apparent effect — and measuring it in this simulator says that at realistic rates it is **small**: on the 452-gene reference design, 0.5 % mis-assignment moves the hit/non-hit separation from 0.799 to 0.794 among the genes that were identifiable to begin with. Deep sequencing averages most of it away.

records.source: Mis-assignment gives a gene phantom reads in wells it never entered, so the covariate the model regresses positive counts on is a shrunk-toward-uniform version of the truth. The obvious consequence is regression dilution — an attenuated coefficient and a smaller apparent effect — and measuring it in this simulator says that at realistic rates it is **small**: on the 452-gene reference design, 0.5 % mis-assignment moves the hit/non-hit separation from 0.799 to 0.794 among the genes that were identifiable to begin with. Deep sequencing averages most of it away.
records.translation: La asignación errónea da a un gen lecturas fantasma en pocillos en los que nunca entró, de modo que la covariable sobre la que el modelo regresa los recuentos de positivos es una versión de la realidad contraída hacia la uniformidad. La consecuencia obvia es la dilución de la regresión (un coeficiente atenuado y un efecto aparente menor), y medirla en este simulador indica que, con tasas realistas, es **pequeña**: en el diseño de referencia de 452 genes, un 0.5 % de asignación errónea mueve la separación entre aciertos y no aciertos de 0.799 a 0.794 entre los genes que eran identificables desde el principio. La secuenciación profunda promedia la mayor parte.

records.context: The consequence that is *not* obvious, and is much larger, is what it does to the genes that were never testable. A gene that landed in every microplate sample position, or in none, has a constant read-fraction column; its coefficient is confounded with the intercept and ``power_model.prepare_model_data`` reports it as unidentified rather than as a non-hit. That check is what keeps a thin design from reporting untestable genes as negative results, and mis-assignment defeats it, because phantom reads give every gene a covariate that *varies*. On the same reference design, 0.5 % error takes the scored library from 317 genes to all 452: the 135 genes that were correctly flagged "untested" become scored non-hits with a covariate made entirely of noise, and the screening experiment-wide separation falls from 0.799 to 0.723 — fourteen times the direct dilution, and all of it from a safeguard being switched off rather than from any loss of signal.

records.translation: La consecuencia que *no* es obvia, y que es mucho mayor, es lo que hace con los genes que nunca pudieron evaluarse. records.source: If ``var`` is negative, or if ``var >= mean * (1 - mean)``. That bound is the variance of the Bernoulli with the same mean and is the supremum over *all* distributions on ``[0, 1]``; no beta reaches it. Note this makes ``mean`` of exactly 0 or 1 admissible only with ``var == 0``. Clamping instead of raising would return a distribution with the wrong spread and, for a classifier accuracy, silently change the effect size the whole power analysis is measuring.
records.translation: Si ``var`` es negativa, o si ``var >= mean * (1 - mean)``. Esa cota es la varianza de la Bernoulli con la misma media y es el supremo sobre *todas* las distribuciones en ``[0, 1]``; ninguna beta la alcanza. Obsérvese que esto hace que un ``mean`` exactamente igual a 0 o 1 solo sea admisible con ``var == 0``. Acotar en lugar de generar una excepción devolvería una distribución con la dispersión equivocada y, para la exactitud de un clasificador, cambiaría en silencio el tamaño del efecto que mide todo el análisis de potencia.

records.context: ``numpy.random.Generator.dirichlet`` draws independent gammas and normalises them. At small concentration the individual gamma draws underflow to exactly ``0.0``, so a gene gets an abundance of exactly zero — measured here, at ``alpha = 0.05`` with 452 categories, numpy produces exact zeros in roughly one draw in ten, and this routine produces none. A zero abundance removes the gene from every well, and the downstream read fraction for that gene becomes ``0 / 0`` in any well where nothing else amplified.

records.source: ``numpy.random.Generator.dirichlet`` draws independent gammas and normalises them. At small concentration the individual gamma draws underflow to exactly ``0.0``, so a gene gets an abundance of exactly zero — measured here, at ``alpha = 0.05`` with 452 categories, numpy produces exact zeros in roughly one draw in ten, and this routine produces none. A zero abundance removes the gene from every well, and the downstream read fraction for that gene becomes ``0 / 0`` in any well where nothing else amplified.
records.translation: ``numpy.random.Generator.dirichlet`` extrae gammas independientes y las normaliza. Con una concentración pequeña, las extracciones gamma individuales se subdesbordan hasta exactamente ``0.0``, de modo que un gen recibe una abundancia exactamente nula; medido aquí, con ``alpha = 0.05`` y 452 categorías, numpy produce ceros exactos aproximadamente en una de cada diez extracciones, y esta rutina no produce ninguno. Una abundancia nula elimina el gen de todos los pocillos, y la fracción de lecturas posterior de ese gen pasa a ser ``0 / 0`` en cualquier pocillo en el que no se amplificó nada más.

records.context: **Where the under-dispersed case is approximate, and which way.** A binomial has an integer number of trials, so it cannot hit an arbitrary ``(mean, var)`` pair. Given the rounded ``n``, the success probability is set to ``mean / n`` so the **mean is exact** and the realised variance is ``mean * (1 - mean/n)``, the nearest value the family attains — within about ``1/n`` relative of the request. The mean is the one preserved because it is the biologically meaningful quantity (cells per well) and it sets the scale of everything downstream, whereas a variance off by a percent changes only how wide the well-to-well spread is. Rounding ``n`` while keeping ``p = (mean - var) / mean`` — the naive inversion — biases the *mean* instead, by up to half a count, which is a systematic error in every well of a sweep.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.sample_count_mean_variance#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Where the under-dispersed case is approximate, and which way.** A binomial has an integer number of trials, so it cannot hit an arbitrary ``(mean, var)`` pair. Given the rounded ``n``, the success probability is set to ``mean / n`` so the **mean is exact** and the realised variance is ``mean * (1 - mean/n)``, the nearest value the family attains — within about ``1/n`` relative of the request. The mean is the one preserved because it is the biologically meaningful quantity (cells per well) and it sets the scale of everything downstream, whereas a variance off by a percent changes only how wide the well-to-well spread is. Rounding ``n`` while keeping ``p = (mean - var) / mean`` — the naive inversion — biases the *mean* instead, by up to half a count, which is a systematic error in every well of a sweep.
records.translation: **Dónde es aproximado el caso infradisperso, y en qué sentido.** Una binomial tiene un número entero de ensayos, por lo que no puede alcanzar un par ``(mean, var)`` arbitrario. Dado el ``n`` redondeado, la probabilidad de éxito se fija en ``mean / n`` para que la **media sea exacta**, y la varianza obtenida es ``mean * (1 - mean/n)``, el valor más cercano que alcanza la familia, a menos de aproximadamente ``1/n`` en términos relativos de lo solicitado. Se conserva la media porque es la magnitud con significado biológico (células por pocillo) y fija la escala de todo lo posterior, mientras que una varianza desviada en un uno por ciento solo cambia la amplitud de la dispersión entre pocillos. Redondear ``n`` manteniendo ``p = (mean - var) / mean`` (la inversión ingenua) sesga en cambio la *media*, hasta en medio recuento, lo que supone un error sistemático en cada pocillo de un barrido.

records.context: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` controls how *even* the library is, and it runs the opposite way from intuition: large alpha gives every gene about ``1/n`` of the pool, alpha near zero concentrates the whole pool on one gene, and ``alpha = 1`` corresponds to a Gini index of 0.5. The real *T. gondii* screening experiment this simulator was fitted to came out at ``alpha = 0.6``, i.e. quite skewed — which is why some genes in it never reached enough microplate sample positions to be callable at all.

records.source: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` controls how *even* the library is, and it runs the opposite way from intuition: large alpha gives every gene about ``1/n`` of the pool, alpha near zero concentrates the whole pool on one gene, and ``alpha = 1`` corresponds to a Gini index of 0.5. The real *T. gondii* screen this simulator was fitted to came out at ``alpha = 0.6``, i.e. quite skewed — which is why some genes in it never reached enough wells to be callable at all.
records.translation: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` controla lo *uniforme* que es la biblioteca, y funciona al contrario de lo que sugiere la intuición: un alpha grande da a cada gen aproximadamente ``1/n`` del conjunto, un alpha cercano a cero concentra todo el conjunto en un solo gen, y ``alpha = 1`` corresponde a un índice de Gini de 0.5. El cribado real de *T. gondii* con el que se ajustó este simulador dio ``alpha = 0.6``, es decir, bastante sesgado, y por eso algunos de sus genes nunca llegaron a suficientes pocillos para poder evaluarse.

records.context: Both imaging and sequencing plates originate from *one shared source*: the spot plate. Thus the genotypes in a well are one physical fact observed twice. records.source: The imaging and sequencing plates are both simulated from the *same* spot plate — which genotypes are in a well is one physical fact, observed twice. Each stage draws from its own spawned child stream, so changing the number of imaging cells does not shift the sequencing draws; that independence is what makes a parameter sweep interpretable, since otherwise every point on the sweep would differ by an unrelated re-randomisation as well as by the parameter.
records.translation: Las placas de imagen y de secuenciación se simulan ambas a partir de la *misma* placa de siembra: qué genotipos hay en un pocillo es un único hecho físico, observado dos veces. Cada etapa extrae de su propio flujo hijo derivado, de modo que cambiar el número de células en imagen no desplaza las extracciones de secuenciación; esa independencia es lo que hace interpretable un barrido de parámetros, ya que de lo contrario cada punto del barrido diferiría por una nueva aleatorización no relacionada además de por el parámetro.

records.context: **Probabilities above 1 are clipped, with a warning.** The Bernoulli probability is a product of two independently drawn quantities and nothing constrains it to ``[0, 1]``; at ``alpha = 0.6`` the most abundant gene's share times a ``mu = 4.6`` microplate sample position factor exceeds 1 routinely. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` there and carries on. This clips to 1 and emits one :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` carrying the number of clipped cells and the largest offending probability, because a clipped run has a realised genes-per-microplate sample position *below* the one that was requested — the answer is still usable, but not for the parameter value written on it.

records.source: **Probabilities above 1 are clipped, with a warning.** The Bernoulli probability is a product of two independently drawn quantities and nothing constrains it to ``[0, 1]``; at ``alpha = 0.6`` the most abundant gene's share times a ``mu = 4.6`` well factor exceeds 1 routinely. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` there and carries on. This clips to 1 and emits one :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` carrying the number of clipped cells and the largest offending probability, because a clipped run has a realised genes-per-well *below* the one that was requested — the answer is still usable, but not for the parameter value written on it.
records.translation: **Las probabilidades superiores a 1 se recortan, con una advertencia.** La probabilidad de Bernoulli es el producto de dos magnitudes extraídas de forma independiente y nada la restringe a ``[0, 1]``; con ``alpha = 0.6``, la proporción del gen más abundante multiplicada por un factor de pocillo de ``mu = 4.6`` supera 1 con frecuencia. El ``rbinom`` de R devuelve ``NA`` en ese caso y continúa. Esto recorta a 1 y emite un único :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` con el número de celdas recortadas y la mayor probabilidad problemática, porque una ejecución recortada tiene un número de genes por pocillo obtenido *inferior* al solicitado: la respuesta sigue siendo utilizable, pero no para el valor de parámetro que lleva escrito.
